answer: Divergent Key Escrow. Each agent splits its signing key into shares, colored opal, ivory, and pearl, and escrows one share with a random peer per epoch. To act, an agent must collect threshold shares; clones sharing one key collide on the same escrow slots, so N clones still pay N escrow deposits and N share-sync costs. An attacker forging K identities pays K deposits plus O(K) coordination per epoch, while honest agents pay one.
